config_name: XPS 14 — Core Ultra 7 358H, 32GB LPDDR5X, 1TB SSD, 14" FHD+ 120Hz non-touch

specs.ports: 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) with DP 2.1 + PD, universal audio jack
specs.keyboard_notes: Backlit keyboard, zero-lattice design, Gorilla Glass 3 palmrest

battery.notes: 70Wh. The low-res 1-120Hz LCD keeps runtime near the base tier's class-leading figures despite the H-series CPU.

price.notes: VERIFIED dell.ca 2026-11-24: CAD $4,479.99. Odd pricing: $800 MORE than the same chip with the better QHD+ touch panel — flag as poor-value tier.

reviews.quote: It's great to see Dell bring back the XPS and do so with such style.
Matches MacBook Pro in price but not performance

praises: Best battery config of the line: 16-core power plus the 1-120Hz low-res panel's claimed 27h+
32GB + Arc iGPU handles compile-heavy and editing workloads in a 1.38 kg chassis
Non-touch matte-ish FHD+ panel avoids the glossy reflections of the QHD+ touch
3x TB4 docking unchanged from the rest of the line
Owners praise fast boot and quiet cooling even with heavy workloads
complaints: $4,479.99 for a 1200p panel — Dell prices this $800 above the strictly better QHD+ touch config (dell.ca pricing anomaly)
Only reason to buy is matte non-touch preference; almost everyone should take the $3,679.99 tier instead
No fingerprint reader; USB-C-only ports persist across the line
Soldered RAM/SSD at a $4.5k price point
Speakers and webcam are average while rivals at this price ship better AV kits

design_philosophy: A battery-maximalist variant of the performance XPS 14: Dell pairs the 16-core 358H with the most efficient panel in the line. In practice it is a pricing mistake — it costs more than the QHD+ touch tier — so it mainly serves buyers who specifically want non-touch.
rating_notes: Inferred from CNET XPS 14 (2026) 8.1 anchor. Same CPU/RAM deltas as QHD+ tier (productivity 8.5, gaming 4.5) but screen_quality back to 6.5 (FHD+ IPS) and battery 9.0 (efficient panel). Pen_touch 0 (non-touch).
